summary: Procure GitHub Copilot for Business seats, migrate contractors off personal subscriptions, and enable SCIM provisioning
description:
Issue summary:
Request to purchase GitHub Copilot for Business for the Engineering org (approx 85 seats) and to migrate ~20 contractors currently using personal Copilot subscriptions to the company tenant. The migration must include SCIM provisioning (via Okta) so seats are provisioned automatically and deprovisioned when contractors end contracts.

Context/Background:
We have increasing usage of Copilot across platform and product teams. Multiple contractors are on personal paid plans which causes billing leakage and security/asset management gaps. Centralizing on a Copilot for Business license will simplify cost tracking, enable org-level policy enforcement, and allow SSO + SCIM lifecycle management.

Requested deliverables:
- Purchase 85 seats of GitHub Copilot for Business (initial), with an option to add 20 contractor seats on the same billing agreement.
- Enable SCIM provisioning with Okta and map contractor groups.
- Migrate contractors off personal subscriptions and reclaim any overlapping seats.
- Ensure billing is charged to ENG-OPS cost center and tagged in finance system.
impact: Untracked spend on personal subscriptions, inconsistent license management, inability to enforce org policies for Copilot usage. Moderate operational risk: onboarding/offboarding of contractors is manual and error-prone.
business_justification: Centralizing Copilot licenses reduces monthly vendor spend (discounted org pricing), enables automatic offboarding via SCIM (reduces security risk), and provides visibility to engineering management for budgeting. Required for standardizing devtools for several upcoming hires and contractor engagements in Q2/Q3.
vendor_contact: GitHub Sales (sales@github.com) / Account rep: Jordan Alvarez
procurement_steps: Confirm final seat count with Platform Eng leads by 2026-03-17
Request formal quote from GitHub with annual and monthly billing options
Procurement to open PO and route to finance for approval
Set up GitHub Organization admin to accept license and enable Copilot for Business
Coordinate with Identity team to configure SCIM connector in Okta and map groups
Plan contractor migration wave (notify contractors, revoke personal subscriptions where appropriate), reclaim seats
Tag billing in finance system and verify monthly invoices against ENG-OPS-CC-4201
seat_swap_plan: Three-wave migration: Wave 1 (10 contractors, low-risk) pilot; Wave 2 (7 contractors) broader migration; Wave 3 (remaining contractors + any late joiners). Each wave includes communication template, seat claim deadline, and 3 business days of support from Platform Eng.
acceptance_criteria: GitHub Copilot for Business purchase confirmed and PO issued
SCIM connector configured and provisioning test succeeds for a sample user
At least 90% of targeted contractors migrated to company seats or confirmed exempt
Finance tags invoices correctly to ENG-OPS-CC-4201 for the first billing cycle
A short migration guide and FAQ published in Confluence and shared with contractors

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Confirmed preference for annual billing with quarterly reconciliation. Will finalize seat counts by 2026-03-17.

2026-03-13 - Identity (Liam O'Connor): Okta SCIM connector steps reviewed. We need org-owner access to enable SCIM and an email verification flow for contractors; estimated 2 business days to test after access granted.
2026-03-14 - Finance (Aisha Rahman): Please include the draft PO number when sending invoice for pre-approval. Also requested vendor W-9 and SOC2 report link for vendor onboarding.

Need legal/finance to confirm reclaim policy for personal accounts. Verified Okta supports SCIM for Copilot; Identity team will request admin access. No outstanding security blockers; vendor SOC2 link requested from finance.
